spec.name: Trend v17
spec.notes: Classic trend signal on trailing returns. Weekly rebalance.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.8, annual return 11%, maximum drawdown 19%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.80 to 1.73 (change -0.06).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.80 to 1.80. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.80 (as submitted, 10 bps: 1.80); it breaks even at above 200 bps with daily turnover 0.01.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.80 against 1.80 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is 3.04 against 1.80 in research, a gap of -1.24.
The best year gives 24% of total P&L (year 2) and calm regimes give 205%; Sharpe is 5.86 in calm and -6.48 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 2 distinct specs; the best of 2 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.04, so the claimed 1.80 becomes 1.76 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 1.86 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean 0.02, 95th percentile 0.55).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.80 to as low as 1.62 (as low as 1.62 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (21 days) give 26% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 28% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
